title: Finding Your Place in Warlpiri
bodyHtml:
Warlpiri is a language spoken by about 3,000 people in Central Australia. The Warlpiri people are originally from the Tanami Desert in Australia's Northern Territory; most still live in that area, but many also live in other parts of Australia. In Warlpiri-speaking communities, such as Lajamanu, Yuendumu, Willowra, and Nyirripi, schools offer bilingual education programs in both Warlpiri and English.

B1. Below are some sentences in Warlpiri, along with English translations. Write the sentences that should go in the two blank spaces.

WarlpiriEnglish
1.Maliki ka marlungka karrimi.The dog is standing on the kangaroo.
2.Maliki ka marlungka nyinami.The dog is sitting on the kangaroo.
3.Maliki ka karntangka karrimi.The dog is standing on the woman.
4.Marlu ka nantuwurla karrimi.The kangaroo is standing on the horse.
5.Karnta ka kuurlurla ngunami.The woman is lying in the school.
6.Maliki ka nantuwurla ngunami.(a)
7.(b)The kangaroo is sitting in the school.

Here are some more sentences. Study them, and then answer the questions below.

WarlpiriEnglish
8.Nantuwu ka yaparranjirla nyinami.The horse is sitting on the teenage boy.
9.Luurnpa ka mardukujarla nyinami.The kingfisher bird is sitting on the woman.
10.Yaparranji ka paarlparla nyinami.The teenage boy is sitting on the calf (of the leg).
11.Mardukuja ka pirlingka ngunami.The woman is lying on the hill.
12.Pirli ka raangka nyinami.The hill is sitting in the clearing.

B2. Two of the Warlpiri words in the following list have the same meaning as each other. Identify these two words: karnta, luurnpa, mardukuja, ngunami, pirli

B3. Answer each of the following questions by writing A or B.

  1. Wati means "man", so "on the man" is: A. watirla   B. watingka
  2. Warlu means "fire", so "in the fire" is: A. warlurla   B. warlungka
  3. Jaaji means "church", so "in the church" is: A. jaajirla   B. jaajingka
  4. Wulpayi means "creek", so "in the creek" is: A. wulpayirla   B. wulpayingka
  5. Ngurra means "home", so "at home" is: A. ngurrarla   B. ngurrangka
  6. Yama means "shade", so "in the shade" is: A. yamarla   B. yamangka

hints.text: Compare the noun on its own with the same noun when it means 'on/in it'. For example marlu 'kangaroo' appears as marlungka, and nantuwu 'horse' appears as nantuwurla. There are two different endings for 'on/in'.

Which ending a noun takes has nothing to do with its meaning — it depends on the shape (the length) of the word. Count the parts of each noun, and remember that a doubled vowel like aa or uu is a long vowel that counts as extra length.

Try it on a word that isn't asked about: pirli 'hill' is pir-li, two short beats, and it becomes pirlingka. yaparranji 'teenage boy' has four beats and becomes yaparranjirla. Now decide where a word like kuurlu (with its long uu) falls.

explanationHtml:
Step 1: Work out the shape of a Warlpiri sentence

Take sentence 1: Maliki ka marlungka karrimi. = 'The dog is standing on the kangaroo.' Comparing with sentences 2 and 3 we can line things up:

  • maliki = 'dog' (the subject comes first)
  • ka = a little word that marks 'is ...-ing' (it appears in every sentence)
  • marlungka = 'on the kangaroo', karntangka = 'on the woman'
  • karrimi = 'is standing', nyinami = 'is sitting', ngunami = 'is lying'

So the order is: subject – ka – place – verb. English uses a separate word ('on', 'in'); Warlpiri glues an ending onto the noun instead. Linguists call such an ending a suffix, and this particular one, meaning 'on/in/at', is called a locative suffix.

Step 2: Two forms of the same suffix

The place words end in two different ways:

  • -ngka: marlu gives marlungka, karnta gives karntangka, pirli gives pirlingka, raa gives raangka
  • -rla: nantuwu gives nantuwurla, kuurlu gives kuurlurla, yaparranji gives yaparranjirla, mardukuja gives mardukujarla, paarlpa gives paarlparla

Meaning can't be the reason — 'on the woman' shows up both as karntangka and as mardukujarla. So the choice must depend on the sound shape of the noun. Two forms of one suffix chosen by sound like this are called allomorphs.

Step 3: Count beats, not just syllables

Count syllables first: mar-lu (2) takes -ngka; nan-tu-wu (3), ya-pa-rran-ji (4), mar-du-ku-ja (4) take -rla. Good start: short words get -ngka, long words get -rla.

But two words break that simple rule: kuu-rlu and paa-rlpa look like 2 syllables yet take -rla, and raa looks like just 1 syllable yet takes -ngka. Notice the doubled vowels: uu, aa are long vowels. A long vowel counts as two 'beats' of length (linguists call a beat a mora). Recount in beats:

  • 2 beats take -ngka: marlu, karnta, pirli, raa (raa = 2 beats all by itself)
  • 3 or more beats take -rla: nantuwu (3), kuurlu (2+1 = 3), paarlpa (2+1 = 3), yaparranji (4), mardukuja (4)

Now every single example fits. (A quick rule of thumb that gets all the B3 items right: two short syllables take -ngka; anything longer, including a long vowel, takes -rla.)

Step 4: Filling the blanks (B1)

(a) Maliki ka nantuwurla ngunami. = maliki 'dog' + ka + nantuwu-rla 'on the horse' + ngunami 'is lying', giving The dog is lying on the horse.

(b) 'The kangaroo is sitting in the school': kangaroo = marlu, school = kuurlu, which takes -rla (from sentence 5), and 'is sitting' = nyinami, giving Marlu ka kuurlurla nyinami.

Step 5: The two synonyms (B2)

Sentence 3 shows karntangka = 'on the woman'; sentence 9 shows mardukujarla = 'on the woman' too. So karnta and mardukuja both mean 'woman'. (luurnpa = 'kingfisher bird', pirli = 'hill', ngunami = 'is lying'.) Many Australian languages have several words for the same thing, sometimes because a word is avoided for cultural reasons or belongs to a special speech style.

Step 6: Applying the rule (B3)

  • i. wa-ti — 2 short beats, so -ngka: watingka = B
  • ii. wa-rlu — 2 beats, so warlungka = B
  • iii. jaa-ji — long aa, so 3 beats, giving jaajirla = A
  • iv. wul-pa-yi — 3 beats, so wulpayirla = A
  • v. ngu-rra — 2 beats, so ngurrangka = B
  • vi. ya-ma — 2 beats, so yamangka = B

Note that clusters like rr, rl, ng are single consonants in Warlpiri spelling, so they don't add beats — only vowel length and extra syllables do.
